one_line: Opposing sovereigns at Karnal and Delhi during the Afsharid invasion and the Mughal Empire’s collapse in 1739.

appearance.age_look: Both appear in their early-to-mid 40s, medium height; Nadir Shah is wiry and battle-hardened, Muhammad Shah is slightly softer-built but dignified.
appearance.face: Nadir has an angular face, sharp nose, tanned complexion, thin moustache with short boxed beard, a small scar on his left cheek, and a focused, hawk-like stare; Muhammad Shah has an oval face, lighter wheat-brown complexion, neatly trimmed thin moustache, kohl-lined large eyes with a contemplative look, and a calm but worried default expression.
appearance.hair: Nadir’s hair is mostly hidden beneath a tall slightly conical steel helmet wrapped at the base with a dark red cloth band, with only short dark sideburns visible; Muhammad Shah has shoulder-length, softly waved black hair, neatly oiled and tucked back under a tall jewelled turban with a central sarpech.
appearance.costume: Nadir Shah wears an era-accurate early-18th-century Iranian field outfit: a long knee-length mail hauberk over a quilted deep-indigo coat with narrow golden-brown edging, a fitted dark-red leather belt with simple brass buckle, loose sand-coloured trousers tucked into mid-calf brown leather riding boots, and a plain polished-steel helmet with nasal bar and a dark red cloth wrapped around its base; he has a simple dark-blue wool cloak draped back from the shoulders; Muhammad Shah wears a Mughal court jama in rich emerald-green silk with fine gold floral buta motifs, the overlapping front tied on the right, a broad maroon silk patka sash with woven gold edge tied at the waist, off-white churidar trousers, and soft red leather mojari shoes; over the jama he has a lightweight cream-coloured fine muslin shawl with a subtle gold border draped over both shoulders, and his tall cylindrical turban is pale gold with thin red stripes and an ornate central sarpech of gold, emerald and ruby-like stones and a white feather.
appearance.signature: Nadir Shah holds a slightly curved Persian shamshir with a simple steel blade, a dark-brown leather-wrapped hilt and plain brass crossguard in his right hand, while Muhammad Shah carries a sheathed Mughal talwar with a dark green scabbard and ornate disc pommel, held upright in his left hand.

ref_desc: Nadir Shah is a wiry, tanned, scar-cheeked man in deep-indigo quilted coat, mail hauberk, sand trousers, brown boots, red-banded steel helmet and dark-blue cloak wielding a simple shamshir, beside Muhammad Shah, a wheat-complexioned ruler in emerald-green gold-patterned jama, maroon sash, cream shawl, pale-gold striped jewelled turban and red mojari holding a sheathed green-scabbarded talwar.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet showing two fixed characters standing side by side: Nadir Shah and Muhammad Shah, both in historically grounded 1739 North Indian–Iranian dress, fully clothed and dignified. Nadir Shah is a wiry, tanned man with an angular scarred face, thin moustache, short boxed beard and intense eyes, wearing a polished steel helmet with nasal bar and a dark red cloth band at its base, a knee-length mail hauberk over a quilted deep-indigo long coat with narrow golden-brown edging, a dark-red leather belt, loose sand-coloured trousers tucked into mid-calf brown leather riding boots, and a plain dark-blue wool cloak pushed back from his shoulders; he grips a simple slightly curved Persian shamshir with a steel blade and dark-brown leather-wrapped hilt in his right hand. Beside him, Muhammad Shah is a slightly softer-built but regal man with wheat-brown complexion, oval face, kohl-lined large eyes, neat thin moustache and a thoughtful expression, his shoulder-length black hair tucked under a tall pale-gold cylindrical turban with thin red stripes, a central jeweled sarpech of gold, emerald and ruby-like stones, and a white feather; he wears an emerald-green silk jama with fine gold floral buta patterns tied on the right, a broad maroon silk patka sash with gold edging at the waist, off-white churidar trousers, red leather mojari shoes, and a cream fine-muslin shawl with a subtle gold border draped over both shoulders while he holds upright in his left hand a sheathed Mughal talwar with a dark green scabbard and ornate disc pommel. Emphasize clear, consistent anime proportions, the contrasting deep indigo, dark red and blue of Nadir’s martial outfit against the emerald green, maroon, pale gold and cream of Muhammad’s courtly costume, and show them front-facing to capture their fixed face shapes, hairstyles, garments and signature weapons for reuse across panels.
